subject: Dedicated capacity: excess-usage playbook, billing fallbacks and SLAs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@nimbuscloud.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: excess-usage playbook, billing fallbacks and SLAs

Hi Jake / Nimbus procurement team,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the transparency on the traffic shape. Based on the telemetry you shared (attached) and the target P50 latency goals you described, I sketched a recommended commercial approach that aims to balance predictability for you with operational headroom for short surges. The high-level proposal is attached (redwood-dedicated-pricing-proposal-2026-09-28.pdf) but the key concepts are below: 

- Commit sizing: contract for a guaranteed pool (example: 80 vGPU-equivalent units) sized to cover your baseline 95th percentile sustained throughput.
- Grace buffer / short burst: allow a transparent 20% burst above commit for up to 45 minutes/day without surcharge (soft buffer). Bursts are rate-limited by graceful throttles to preserve QoS for committed tenants.
- Metering granularity + surcharge: above the grace buffer, meter excess consumption as vGPU-minutes billed in the monthly true-up at $0.28 per vGPU-minute (or an equivalent per-1000-token rate we can map). We can also offer a step-down price for partners who commit to a 12-month renewal.
- Throttle behavior: prefer a soft-throttle path (token-bucket style) with clear E2E SLO signals; hard cutoffs only under sustained 6+ hour overruns or capacity exhaustion.
- Settlement mechanics: monthly reconciliation with automated credits for documented platform incidents that caused higher-than-expected usage.

Questions for you: would Nimbus accept a 20%/45min grace buffer, or do you need a different burst envelope? Are you comfortable with vGPU-minute metering for excess or would a per-token surcharge better match your internal chargebacks?

I copied Dylan (SE) and Laura (Account Lead) — Dylan can follow up on the runtime implications and sample throttling profile. If this shape looks reasonable, we can sketch contract language (SLA appendix + true-up table) for your procurement team to review.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing-proposal-2026-09-28.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
Attachment: nimbus-usage-telemetry.csv (CSV, 230KB)

From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbuscloud.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: excess-usage playbook, billing fallbacks and SLAs

Marissa — thanks for the proposal and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from procurement/infra: 

1) The 20% / 45min buffer is promising; can we make the daily budget aggregate across pools (we have dev and prod pools that can spike at different times)?
2) vGPU-minute billing is fine, but we need clearer visibility into how minutes are calculated (queued vs active compute). Can Dylan outline the exact metering model?
3) For SLAs: we need a clause that if Redwood’s autoscaling or misrouting causes sustained excess for >3 hours, Nimbus receives a pro-rated credit and no overage charge for that window.

Also — if we accept a 12-month commit, what incremental discount do we get on the above-commit rate?

Jake
Procurement Lead — Nimbus Cloud
Attachment: nimbus-usage-telemetry.csv (re-sent)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@nimbuscloud.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: excess-usage playbook, billing fallbacks and SLAs

Hi Jake — quick technical note on metering and throttling so procurement and infra can line this up with their internal chargeback model.

Metering model we propose: bill vGPU-minutes only for "active" runtime (GPU scheduling slot in use). We do not bill for queued requests waiting >30s for a free executor; instead those requests are subject to the soft-throttle policy that pushes them into a short retry window.

Throttling/overage behavior (practical):
- Soft-throttle: token-bucket algorithm that reduces new token issuance when pool usage > commit + grace. This preserves in-flight streams (no abrupt cut) and sheds low-priority work first.
- Escalation to hard-throttle: if consumption is > commit + grace for 3 continuous hours AND we cannot provision burst capacity, we will flip to a hard cap to protect overall cluster health.
- Incident-driven credit: if the overage was caused by us (misrouting, autoscaler bug, kernel regression), we zero-rate the excess window and issue a credit.

On numbers: for your telemetry, the mapping we'd use is: 1 vGPU-minute ~= 60 * effective_tokens_per_second / factor. For contract simplicity we can present a table that maps common 1k TPS request patterns to vGPU-minutes so your FinOps can forecast.

Happy to run a 48-hour simulated traffic replay on a staging pool if you want to validate the charge model.

— Dylan
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: throttling-behavior-diagram.png (PNG, 72KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@nimbuscloud.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: excess-usage playbook, billing fallbacks and SLAs

Jake — following up on the commercial levers: if Nimbus signs a 12-month reserved commit at 80 vGPU-equivalents we can tier the above-commit rate as follows (negotiable):

- 0–10% above grace: $0.28 per vGPU-minute
- 10–30% above grace: $0.20 per vGPU-minute
- >30% above grace: $0.12 per vGPU-minute (applies only if you accept a floor monthly true-up)

Alternatively, we can offer a capped monthly overage ceiling (example: no more than 25% of the committed monthly spend) for an additional 5% on the committed fee. That gives you predictability for worst-case spikes.

We propose contract language: monthly true-up with 30-day dispute window, platform-incident carveouts, and a clearly enumerated "burst definition" (burst = sustained > commit for >5 minutes and < 3 hours).

If that sounds good, Marissa / I can get a draft SOW and appendix to legal for redlines.

— Laura
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-steps-table.csv (CSV, 6KB)

From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@nimbuscloud.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: excess-usage playbook, billing fallbacks and SLAs

Laura / Marissa — appreciate the concrete tiers. A few commitments from our side and next asks: 

1) We can do 12-month commit at 80 vGPU-equivalents if the overage ceiling option is included (capped monthly overage at 20% of committed spend) and the hard-throttle sanity check is moved to 6 hours (we prefer a longer soft-fail window).
2) We need clear telemetry hooks: a daily CSV export of pool-level vGPU-minute consumption and a webhook for any hard-throttle events.
3) Please add contract language that defines "platform incident" (examples: autoscaler misassignment, kernel OOM) and the remediation timeline (72 hours to investigate, credit issued within 30 days).

If Redwood can add those three items, we are ready to move to legal review and target a signature by Oct 20.

Jake Turner
Procurement Lead — Nimbus Cloud
Attachment: signed-intent-nimbus-2026-10-02.txt (text, 1KB)
